kakekotoba.reading_primary: おうさか (place name, Ōsaka barrier)
kakekotoba.interaction: The place name Ōsaka literally contains 逢ふ 'to meet/encounter,' so the barrier's name itself enacts the poem's theme: all who go, return, part, know one another or don't, nonetheless 'meet' (逢ふ) at this checkpoint — the toponym is simultaneously a literal location and a statement of universal encounter.

jokotoba.pivot: こそ/や rhetorical exclamation pointing forward to the scene described
jokotoba.function: An emphatic demonstrative opening ('Is this the very...') that does not itself carry sound-based imagery but rhetorically frames and heightens the entire following description, functioning like a preface pointing to the famous scene of the Ōsaka barrier — included here loosely though it is closer to pure rhetorical emphasis than a conventional image-preface.

kigo.note: This poem contains no seasonal imagery; it is a philosophical/scenic poem about human comings and goings at a famous barrier, classed among the 雑 (miscellaneous) rather than seasonal poems.

bipartite.kami_theme: The ceaseless traffic of travelers going and returning, and the fact that all such journeys involve partings
bipartite.shimo_theme: Both those who know each other and those who are strangers alike converge and meet at the Ōsaka barrier
bipartite.pivot_note: The kami-no-ku sets up parallel pairs of opposites (going/returning, parting) building toward a universalizing statement; the shimo-no-ku resolves this into a further pair of opposites (acquaintance/stranger) and then collapses all distinctions into the single unifying image of the barrier itself, whose name 逢坂 (Meeting Hill) enacts the reconciliation of all these dualities — kami enumerates human separations, shimo reveals the place where all such separations paradoxically become 'meetings.' This is best described as a cumulative-paradox structure: parting and meeting coincide at the named site.

source_jp:
これやこの
行くも帰るも
別れては
知るも知らぬも
逢坂の関
